title: secrets-mesh-zero-trust-terraform-implementation-notes-v0-1-wip
content:
Summary:

Working notes for a Zero-Trust Secrets Mesh (ZTSM) design and Terraform implementation for on‑prem/VPC private deployments. This doc focuses on the integration surface for HSM/KMS, secrets handling primitives, upgrade/compatibility considerations, and an operational rollout + rollback plan. Intentionally pragmatic: module interfaces, example snippets, test cases, and TODOs for security review.

Goals:
- Provide a Terraform-first module set for deploying a secrets mesh control plane + per-node agents into customer VPCs or air‑gapped clusters.
- Integrate with customer HSM (PKCS#11 / vendor SDK) or cloud KMS as key‑wrapping backends.
- Support robust audit logging (immutable ledger + syslog export) and emergency key rotation workflows.
- Enable canary upgrades with minimal blast radius and clear rollback paths.

Non‑Goals:
- Implementing a full service-mesh for application traffic (we rely on customer's network policies or Anthos/ISTIO where present).
- Replacing customer key ceremonies — we provide tooling hooks, not prescriptive ceremonies.

High-Level Architecture:
- Control plane (ZTSM-controller): runs in customer VPC (or on-prem management plane). Responsible for policy, key lifecycle orchestration, RBAC, and audit collection.
- Node agent (ztsm-agent): lightweight daemon on inference nodes. Handles local envelope encryption, caching, and attestation to control plane.
- HSM-Adapter: sidecar or gateway that talks PKCS#11 -> HTTP for the control plane. Optional if customer uses cloud KMS.
- Audit-collector: append-only event ledger (WORM) implemented as an immutable object storage prefix + signed manifests; syslog/ELK forwarding for enterprise.

Threat model (brief):
- Protect keys at rest (HSM-backed KEKs).
- Minimize plaintext secret exposure on nodes (agent-only ephemeral cache, memory sanitization).
- Ensure strong identity: mTLS between agent <-> control plane + node attestation (TPM/awk attestation when available).

Terraform module notes (interface sketch):
- Module: redwood/ztsm/control-plane (v0.1)
  - variables (recommended):
    - control_plane_cidr (string) -- network range for cp endpoints
    - hsm_backend (string) -- "none" | "pkcs11" | "cloud-kms"
    - hsm_config (map) -- vendor-specific (socket path, module path, slot id)
    - kms_key_alias (string) -- for cloud KMS scenarios
    - audit_bucket_name (string)
    - agent_image (string)
    - allowed_admin_cidrs (list)
  - outputs:
    - control_plane_endpoint (string)
    - service_account_email (string)
    - kms_wrapping_key_id (string)

- Module: redwood/ztsm/agent (v0.1)
  - variables:
    - cluster_id (string)
    - agent_token_secret (string) -- created by control-plane module
    - node_role (string) -- inference | infra | admin
    - cache_size_mb (number)
  - outputs:
    - agent_daemonset_name (string)

Implementation notes / gotchas:
- PKCS#11: many vendors change slot numbering across firmware updates. Module should accept both slot ID and token label and include a discovery script executed during provisioning. Documented in migration notes.
- HSM client libraries often require glibc version constraints for on‑prem appliance images. Add module sanity checks (node pool OS version).
- Terraform provider ordering: control-plane must run before agent bootstrap tokens are created. Use explicit depends_on to avoid race conditions in CI.

Sample usage snippet (example, not exact syntax):

resource "redwood_ztsm_control_plane" "cp" {
  control_plane_cidr = var.cp_cidr
  hsm_backend = "pkcs11"
  hsm_config = {
    module_path = "/usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so"
    token_label = "REDCUST-HSM"
    slot        = "auto"
  }
  audit_bucket_name = "redwood-cust-logs-prod"
}

Upgrade plan (recommended phased approach):
1) Dev sandbox: deploy control-plane with softHSM and agent on 1-2 nodes. Run basic smoke tests (encrypt/decrypt, agent attestation).
2) Staging: enable HSM adapter with a replica set of adapters (n=3), test PKCS#11 edge cases, and run load test at 2x expected throughput.
3) Canary: upgrade 5% of production nodes to new agent version + control-plane flags. Monitor error rate, latency p50/p95 for token requests.
4) Full rollout: 24h guarded rollout with staggered batches, monitor audit logs for anomalies and growth in KMS usage (cost gating).

Rollback strategy (explicit):
- Control plane changes must be backwards compatible for agent API contracts. If a control-plane change is incompatible, deploy a compat shim that supports both v1/v2 endpoints for 48h.
- Agent rollback: retain previous agent container image in registry and perform a controlled daemonset rollout -y.
- HSM adapter failures: automatic fallback to wrapped-keys served from control plane cache (short-lived) for up to 30 minutes while adapters recover.

Testing matrix (must pass before production):
- PKCS#11 discovery & slot change between firmware versions (test 1,2,3)
- HSM outage simulation: HSM down for 5/15/60 minutes -> ensure agent fallback and audit events emitted
- Network partition: agent cannot reach control plane for 10m -> verify local cache TTL and deny-by-default refresh behavior

Audit logging & retention:
- Events to capture: key-create, key-wrap, key-unwrap, admin-rotate, agent-attest (success/fail), token-issue, token-revoke, HSM-adapter-error.
- Immutable ledger: write event manifests to an append-only prefix (S3 or on-prem object store) and periodically sign a Merkle-root manifest with the HSM private signing key.
- Retention policy: default 365d (configurable to 7y for regulated customers). Provide a legal-hold flag that prevents deletion and triggers alerts to security@redwood.com.
- Forwarding: canonical syslog + structured JSON events to customers' log collector (support GELF/JSON over TLS).

Emergency key rotation runbook (TL;DR):
1) Generate new KEK in HSM (or cloud KMS) with new key metadata id.
2) Rewrap application data keys: control-plane issues a background job to re‑wrap active key‑records to new KEK, marking previous KEK in "deprecating" state.
3) Stagger agent config reload: agents fetch new wrapping metadata and start writing new keys wrapped under KEK-v2.
4) After 48h of validation, retire KEK-v1 (move to revoked state and archive metadata).

Operational telemetry (what we must expose in Console/Datadog):
- KMS request rate (per-key, per-customer)
- Agent cache hit ratio
- Latency histogram for wrap/unwrap ops
- Audit-event ingestion lag
- HSM adapter health (uptime per adapter)

Hardening checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] mTLS enforced for all control-plane <-> agent traffic
- [ ] Node attestation enabled (TPM/SEV when available)
- [ ] Minimum agent process capabilities: drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN, restrict file system mount access
- [ ] Memory-scrubbing on secret eviction (lang: go; use explicit runtime zeroing)
- [ ] Hardened signer path: signer key stays in HSM and never exported
- [ ] Signed manifests for audit ledgers with HSM key material

Migration / compatibility notes (things we've seen in the field):
- SoftHSM behaves differently from vendor HSMs for token labels -> provide discovery + fallback in tests.
- Some customers run HSM appliances that require IP allowlisting; ensure Terraform outputs include required IPs for provisioning windows.
- Firmware upgrades occasionally rotate device cert chain; coordinate with customer before firmware upgrades and include rolling test plan.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Design a simple UI flow in Console for emergency rotation that orchestrates steps 1..4 above and shows preflight checks.
- Should we provide an operator cronjob for automatic audit manifest signing or mandate manual ceremonies? (security preference?)
- Decide default audit retention and legal-hold UX for Console.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands
- Force agent to clear cache and re-attest:
  curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" ${CP_ENDPOINT}/api/v1/nodes/${NODE_ID}/restart-attest

- Validate PKCS#11 module (on host):
  p11tool --list-tokens --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so

- Emergency unwrap (manual):
  # Only for SRE with access and audit entry
  openssl rsautl -decrypt -inkey /tmp/tmp-unwrapped.pem -in wrapped_blob.bin -out plaintext_key.bin

Notes to reviewers: this is an early draft targeted at infra engineers + partner SREs. Feedback please on the Terraform module boundaries and the fallbacks we propose for HSM outages.
